title: Theo and the Colony
premise: Hazel Eastwick smuggles forbidden memories through orbital customs, and among her contraband she discovers a recording of Meridian Colony's slow, deliberate abandonment — a station the Consortium wrote off while two thousand colonists still breathed. When the manifest of the never-flown ship Perihelion lists a name that shouldn't exist — Theo Voss, Hazel's dead brother — she and her partner Juno trace it to Meridian and find the colony alive in cryosleep, but with power for only half of them to wake. The choice of who survives was rigged years ago by the same officials who abandoned the colony, and Theo's name is the key to exposing them. In the end, Hazel sacrifices her own memory archive — every recording she's ever smuggled, including her memories of Theo — to broadcast the truth and reroute power to wake everyone, waking to a world where she must learn to love the people she saved without remembering why she fought for them.
about_author: Emrys Hartwell is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to transmissions from ships that never came home. They write science fiction about people who keep records no one asked them to keep.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Hazel Eastwick runs memory-chips past orbital customs aboard the freighter Kestrel, hiding grief-recordings inside shipping manifests. Her partner Juno handles the bribes; Hazel handles the ghosts. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: establish her loneliness and the quiet intimacy of carrying other people's most precious memories for money.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: A black-market broker sells Hazel a corrupted data-slate: the flight manifest of the Perihelion, a colony ship officially destroyed before launch. One name stops her cold — Theo Voss, her brother, dead eleven years. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: shock curdling into obsession as grief reopens an old wound.

chapters.title: Juno's Rules
chapters.summary: Juno warns Hazel against chasing ghosts; names on dead manifests get smugglers killed. But Juno's own hesitation reveals they recognize the Perihelion's registry code. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: tension between self-preservation and loyalty, hinting Juno knows more than they admit.

chapters.title: What the Chip Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel decodes the slate's hidden layer: not a manifest but a memory-recording from Meridian Colony, documenting life support failing while Consortium ships pass by without answering distress calls. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: horror at witnessing an abandonment no one was meant to see.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: The Kestrel diverts toward Meridian's coordinates under cover of a salvage contract. En route, Hazel confesses that Theo didn't die in an accident — he vanished investigating Consortium shipping routes. POV: alternating Hazel/Juno. Emotional beat: partners becoming co-conspirators, trust deepening under risk.

chapters.title: Lights in a Dead Station
chapters.summary: Meridian appears derelict, but thermal scans show cryo-bays still drawing power. Two thousand sleepers, sustained by a failing reactor on borrowed time. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: awe and dread — the forgotten are not gone, only waiting.

chapters.title: Theo Voss, Alive
chapters.summary: In the cryo-bay's index, Theo's pod shows active status. Before Hazel can reach it, station defenses lock down the bay — someone has been maintaining this place. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into urgency, then blocked by an unseen hand.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: They meet Wren Adeyemi, the sole awake caretaker, who has kept two thousand people alive alone for six years. She recognizes the Perihelion manifest and explains: the ship never flew because its passengers were diverted here to die quietly. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: exhaustion meeting relief — she is no longer alone.

chapters.title: Half a Humanity
chapters.summary: Wren reveals the reactor can safely wake only half the colonists. The wake-list was authored by Consortium Director Ilsa Marchetti — and it excludes anyone who knew about the diversion. Theo's name is on the list of the condemned. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; survival recast as an act of violence.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Hazel realizes Theo's memory-recordings, which she's been smuggling for years, contain evidence of Marchetti's order. The contraband she carried unknowingly was the case against him. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: bitter irony — she profited from the proof that could save her brother.

chapters.title: Juno's Debt
chapters.summary: Juno finally confesses: years ago they sold route information to Marchetti's office, never knowing what it was for. Their guilt funded their escape from the trade. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: shame laid bare; the theme of complicity made personal.

chapters.title: Customs Comes Calling
chapters.summary: A Consortium inspection vessel arrives at Meridian, tipped off by Hazel's own customs contact. The trio must hide the truth of the occupied station or lose everything. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread as the net tightens.

chapters.title: Marchetti
chapters.summary: Director Ilsa Marchetti boards personally. She offers Hazel a deal: walk away rich, and Theo stays asleep forever — safe, preserved, erased. POV: Marchetti. Emotional beat: chilling pragmatism; the antagonist believes she is merciful.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Hazel refuses. Juno begs her to take the deal — one life against two thousand, and their own necks. Their partnership fractures in the cryo-bay's blue light beside Theo's pod. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: heartbreak; love tested against duty and losing, for now.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Plan
chapters.summary: Wren proposes hijacking Meridian's long-range array to broadcast the colony's records — but the transmission requires the reactor's reserve power, killing hundreds of sleepers to buy the signal time. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grim arithmetic; every option costs lives.

chapters.title: Hazel's Archive
chapters.summary: Hazel offers her own solution: her smuggled memory-archive holds enough encrypted bandwidth to carry the evidence if she wipes it entirely — every recording, including her memories of Theo. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; she chooses strangers' futures over her own past.

chapters.title: The Last Recording
chapters.summary: Before the wipe, Hazel plays Theo's final message, meant for her all along: he found the diversion plot and let himself be taken so the evidence would survive in transit. He trusted the smugglers' network to carry it home. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: catharsis and resolve; grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Seizure
chapters.summary: Marchetti's marines storm the station. Juno, choosing Hazel over safety, sabotages the boarding locks and buys the trio minutes. Wren begins the transfer; Hazel jacks her archive into the array. POV: Juno. Emotional beat: redemption under fire; duty realigned with love.

chapters.title: Everything We Kept
chapters.summary: Climax. As marines breach the bay, the broadcast fires — Meridian's records, Marchetti's orders, and Hazel's entire archive streaming to every relay in the system. Hazel watches her memories of Theo dissolve into signal. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: sacrifice at full cost, witnessed in real time.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Signal
chapters.summary: The broadcast goes public. Consortium ships divert to Meridian; Marchetti is arrested by her own security detail as the evidence spreads faster than it can be suppressed. The reactor stabilizes on emergency resupply. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: exhausted vindication; the forgotten are remembered at last.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: All two thousand pods open. Theo wakes to a sister who saved his life but cannot remember his face. He carries her recordings — she archived copies of everything except herself — and begins telling her their story back. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: bittersweet reunion; love outliving memory.

chapters.title: The Colony Remembers
chapters.summary: Months later, Meridian rebuilds. Hazel, learning her own history secondhand, chooses to stay rather than return to the smuggling lanes. Juno ferries supplies; Wren plants the first new garden. Some things, Hazel writes in her first fresh recording, are worth forgetting yourself for. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: resolution — identity rebuilt not from memory but from choice.
